messages:
acme-sre: Hey, after we moved traffic behind an NLB + Istio in our VPC, our app starts getting 401s. Looks like the app is not seeing the Authorization header anymore. This only happens for SSO flows using the opaque session cookie -> bearer rewrite. Root cause?

maria: Can you paste a minimal request/response? Is the 401 from our app or from an upstream authz service?

acme-sre: 401 from our backend service (token validation fails). We capture the incoming request at the backend and the header is either missing or truncated (half the cookie string). Example (from tcpdump at backend):

acme-sre: ```
GET /api/v1/submit HTTP/1.1
Host: svc.internal
X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.2.14
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJ...truncated-part
Cookie: _acmesess=opaque-blob-part1; other=...
```

aj: Truncated header is odd. Two quick checks: 1) Are you terminating TLS at the NLB or passing through? 2) Are you using proxy-protocol? NLB + proxy-protocol + Istio can cause header fragmentation if an intermediate L7 proxy rewrites cookie->auth header.

acme-sre: TLS is terminated at our ALB in another region -> but here NLB is a TCP passthrough in the VPC. We do have PROXY protocol enabled on the NLB. We also have an EnvoyFilter that converts the opaque cookie into `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header for the mesh.

maria: That EnvoyFilter transformation is the most likely place. If the filter does `remove_cookie` + `add_header` but the header value exceeds some internal buffer boundary it can get split across TCP segments and the receiving side (Envoy on the pod) may treat it as two header fragments and drop/trim. Did you enable large_headers in Envoy?

acme-sre: We didn't touch large headers. Default seems to be 8KB, and our cookie is ~6KB. It should fit. But the truncation is ~3KB, weird.

ingrid: @maria any known interactions with PROXY protocol + EnvoyFilter header rewrites? I remember a case where the PROXY line incorrectly appended newline sequences that made the header parser think the header ended early.

aj: Yes — older Envoy versions had issues when PROXY protocol v1 lines and custom header rewrites combined with a mis-ordered filter chain. Two reproducer ideas: 1) curl through NLB with proxy-proto header and replicate cookie length, 2) inject a small Lua filter to log raw header bytes right before the rewrite so we can see the exact bytes Envoy receives.

acme-sre: Repro steps I'm running now: in their VPC, send a request from a bastion that hits the NLB, have NLB forward to Istio ingressgateway, and let our custom envoyfilter swap cookie->bearer.

acme-sre: curl example we used: ```
curl -v -k --resolve svc.example:443:10.0.2.10 \
  -H "Cookie: _acmesess=$(python -c 'print(\"A\"*6000)')" \
  https://svc.example/api/v1/submit
```

maria: Can you also run tcpdump on the istio-ingressgateway pod to verify the raw packet payload? If the Authorization header is truncated before it reaches the mesh, problem is upstream (NLB/proxy-proto). If it shows full header at ingress but truncated at backend, problem is the filter chain in the mesh.

acme-sre: Good point. I ran tcpdump at ingress: full header present. At pod side (service) it's truncated. So ingress had full header, the mesh rewrite must be damaging it.

aj: Two suspects: 1) our EnvoyFilter Lua transform is using concatenation that inadvertently inserts null bytes when handling very long cookie strings, 2) our cluster is on Envoy 1.18 and there was a known header-value copy bug fixed in 1.20. Which Envoy version is your mesh on?

acme-sre: Istio control plane version is 1.16, sidecars are 1.16 (Envoy ~1.18).

maria: OK that aligns. Workarounds: downgrade the rewrite to a header-preserving path (e.g., write bearer token into a custom header `x-acme-bearer` and let the app read that) or upgrade Istio/Envoy to pick up the header copy fix. Short term we can also base64-encode the cookie value during rewrite to avoid parser edge cases and decode in-app.

acme-sre: Can you recommend an EnvoyFilter snippet to switch to `x-acme-bearer`? We prefer to avoid the full Istio upgrade until later.

aj: Paste this EnvoyFilter (note: we keep it minimal):
```
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: acme-cookie-to-bearer
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels:
      app: istio-ingressgateway
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
    match:
      context: GATEWAY
    patch:
      operation: INSERT_BEFORE
      value:
        name: envoy.lua
        typed_config:
          "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
          inlineCode: |
            function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
              local c = request_handle:headers():get("cookie")
              if c then
                local token = string.match(c, "_acmesess=([^;]+)")
                if token then
                  -- write to x-acme-bearer to avoid touching Authorization parsing
                  request_handle:headers():add("x-acme-bearer", token)
                end
              end
            end
```

maria: That avoids touching `Authorization` so Envoy won't do the expensive reparse. Have the app check `x-acme-bearer` and internally validate. Also add a short-lived rollout: canary to a subset of ingress pods to verify no regressions.

acme-sre: Thanks — deployed a canary ingress with the Lua filter and app reading `x-acme-bearer`. Initial tests show no truncation, requests succeed.

ingrid: Great. Action items: 1) acme-sre will keep canary for 48h and collect metrics, 2) we (support + eng-infra) will prioritise an Istio/Envoy upgrade path or backport fix for 1.16, 3) add a KB entry explaining proxy-proto + header-rewrite pitfalls and the x-acme-bearer workaround.

maria: I'll open an internal ENG-INFRA ticket with logs and tcpdumps and link to this thread. Suggest labeling it `authz-header-fragmentation` and target to triage next week.

support-bot: Ticket created: #INFRA-4821 "authz-header-fragmentation - NLB + Istio cookie->bearer rewrite" assigned to aj.

acme-sre: thanks all, appreciate the quick turnaround. Will ping if anything flares up. :thumbsup:
